First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta 
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sinh}⁡\theta \operatorname{cosh}⁡\theta 
$$

 

Letting $\theta =7x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sinh}⁡14x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡7x\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x\,⇒\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡14x=\operatorname{sinh}⁡7x\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡7x(2-\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (2\operatorname{sinh}⁡7x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡7x\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{sinh}⁡7x-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡14x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡7x\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡14x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{7}\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{14}\operatorname{cosh}⁡14x+C \\  & =\frac{2}{7}\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x-\frac{1}{28}\operatorname{cosh}⁡14x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}(2\operatorname{cosh}⁡7x-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cosh}⁡14x)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
